items.prompt: Models get better at drafting. What happens to the cost of checking what they draft?

choices.text: It falls by the same amount
It disappears once the model is good enough

falls.note: This assumes checking got the same discount as claiming. In the essay it did not: a skilled person still spends hours.

vanishes.note: This treats a better-shaped claim as a checked one. A right claim and a wrong one can look identical on the page.

source.quote: Verification did not get the discount.

items.prompt: What does the essay call review debt?

choices.text: The gap between the cost of claiming and the cost of checking
The time a model spends drafting
A journal's queue of papers waiting for review

drafting.note: Drafting is the cheap side. The debt is what checking costs beyond it.

backlog.note: A queue is one place the debt shows up. The debt itself is the cost gap, wherever it lands.

source.quote: That gap between the cost of claiming and the cost of checking is a debt.

items.prompt: When nobody checks, who ends up paying review debt?

choices.text: Whoever has the least power to refuse it
The company that made the model
Nobody, as long as the output looks right

maker.note: The essay traces the bill downhill: to the person debugging at two in the morning, the unpaid reviewer, the clerk, the patient.

nobody.note: Looking right is the shape of a claim. The debt is still there, with a hidden invoice.

source.quote: it always lands on the person with the least power to refuse it

items.prompt: From which side can the gap close?

choices.text: The checking side: make the check cheap to rerun

claiming.note: Better models lower the cost of claiming and leave checking where it was, so the gap grows.

both.note: Every gain on the claiming side widens the gap. Only cheaper checking narrows it.

source.quote: The gap can close only from the verification side.
